measurements.method: Compared the structural wall polygon built from the official feature ring using the repository transform; facade details and entrance are excluded from plan comparison
measurements.after_structural_shell: Walls follow all 16 distinct official source-ring vertices. A new gable roof and portico are architectural additions and extend beyond the wall footprint.
measurements.position_status: The structural footprint follows official FID 224 after the approximate project conversion. Source positional uncertainty is unpublished; entrance side uses visual reference context and remains approximate.
measurements.plan_dimension_status: Walls use official campus GIS feature polygon; the map polygon is not a surveyed wall outline. Roof eaves and entrance portico are estimated.
measurements.orientation_status: Roof ridge follows the footprint long axis; entrance faces the west-side edge selected by the build script. No georeferenced photo confirms this orientation.
measurements.height_status: Unverified estimate: 11.4 m wall height plus 1.4 m roof rise, giving about 12.82 m to the modeled ridge. The official four-level attribute is not a height measurement.
measurements.storey_count_interpretation: The exterior photo shows approximately three above-grade facade levels and a Purdue renovation-study floor plan explicitly labels a Schleman basement (page 78). This makes three visible floors plus one basement a plausible reconciliation of GIS NUM_LEVELS=4, but the GIS counting convention and any basement exposure remain unverified.

geometry_edits: Preserved the official campus GIS structural wall polygon and the existing asset object, collection, scene, ID and file path.
Replaced the flat cap with a shallow red-tile gable roof aligned to the footprint long axis.
Added a paired-glass entry under a portico with brick columns, limestone bases and capitals, a red roof canopy and limestone inscription panel.
Adjusted window bays to avoid overlap with the entrance; three visible facade levels are modeled, while the official GIS four-level attribute remains unresolved.
uncertainties: The official campus GIS polygon is not a certified survey and publishes no positional or dimensional uncertainty.

A Purdue study confirms an interior basement level, making the four-level GIS count plausible alongside three visible above-grade floors. The plan does not establish the GIS counting convention or how much basement is exposed at grade.
The wall height, 1.4 m roof rise, gable shape, portico dimensions and entrance location are estimates, not measured elevations.
The 2024 renovation context may affect current interior use; this model uses the visible exterior reference and does not reproduce recent interior changes.
No independent grader has reviewed this revision.
